newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends off 1,000 stg after late struggle.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends off 1,000 stg after late struggle.

text.p: London cocoa futures advanced to fight the nearby barrier of 1,000 stg in late dealings on Wednesday, but resigned to close just below it.
Gains followed a high opening call as light trade orders and arbitrage fuelled the benchmark March contract to whisk past 1,000, but technical resistance held as expected.
Chart analysts said the market could struggle to vault 1,000 stg, but support seemed well built at 985 while selling pressure was diminishing.
Origin sellers, who have been injecting a daily dose of cocoa every day in response to a strong sterling have backed off, allowing the market to recover the losses.
But sentiment was fragile ahead of Ivorian port arrivals due to begin anytime this week or next week, traders said.
A crop of one million tonnes is forecast this season, only marginally lower than last year's record of 1.2 million.
March ended seven stg higher on the day at 999 stg a tonne after hitting a session high of 1,006 stg. Front-month December put on eight stg to close at 973.
Turnover was a moderate 5,291 lots, most of it on outrights. On the switches, Dec/March traded at 29 stg and March/March and May/May were at 55 stg.
Traders shrugged off a forecast by the USDA on Tuesday which put the world cocoa output at 2.66 million tonnes, down from 2.88 million last season.
